scenarios.ansi: Inrush / energization detection; differential supervision; switching logic
scenarios.l1: No sustained fault declaration; energization/start state recognized
scenarios.l2: CB CLOSE → energization → transient → stable state
scenarios.l3: Initial asymmetric magnetizing current followed by decay; no sustained fault signature
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated inrush/start signal missing: CB-close timestamp + current waveform asymmetry/decay + voltage recovery + absence of persistent fault

scenarios.l1: Inrush indication if available; differential may transiently respond
scenarios.l2: CB CLOSE → current surge → protection response/blocking → reset/stable state
scenarios.l3: Large asymmetric/distorted magnetizing current, decay after energization; harmonics if available
scenarios.fallback: If inrush bit/harmonic channel missing: waveform timing + asymmetry + decay + CB close; harmonic evidence is supporting, not mandatory

scenarios.ansi: Transformer differential; phase OC; distance where applicable
scenarios.l1: Differential/phase protection operates with phase information if available
scenarios.l2: Protection pickup → trip → lockout/master trip if applicable → transformer CB(s) open
scenarios.l3: Sustained differential/fault current, affected phase voltage depression
scenarios.fallback: If differential signal missing: phase OC + both-side currents + voltages + topology + neighboring relay evidence

scenarios.l2: Earth-fault pickup → trip → breaker opening
scenarios.l3: Residual/neutral current and phase-earth voltage behavior
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated earth/REF signal missing: derive residual current from three-phase currents + neutral current if available + topology

scenarios.ansi: Phase/earth OC; directional OC; transformer differential restraint
scenarios.l1: OC/earth protection may operate; differential should normally restrain
scenarios.l2: External feeder/bus protection sequence → transformer protection response → breaker clearing
scenarios.l3: High through-current on both sides with differential current restrained relative to through-current
scenarios.fallback: If restraint/differential data unavailable: compare both-side currents, direction, sequence components, voltage depression and topology

scenarios.scenario: Differential operation caused by CT saturation / measurement issue
scenarios.l1: Differential operates without convincing internal-fault declaration from independent evidence
scenarios.l2: Differential trip occurs during external/high-current event
scenarios.l3: High through-current + distorted/clipped CT waveform + temporary current mismatch
scenarios.fallback: If CT saturation flag unavailable: raw waveform distortion + both-side current comparison + external fault sequence

scenarios.l2: Pickup → timer/alarm/trip → system response
scenarios.l3: Elevated V/Hz; voltage and frequency relationship supports event
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated stage/frequency signal missing: derive V/Hz from voltage waveform and frequency

scenarios.l2: Thermal pickup → delay → alarm/trip → load change
scenarios.l3: Sustained RMS current and/or temperature rise
scenarios.fallback: If thermal element unavailable: RMS current trend + RTD/temperature + loading duration

scenarios.l1: Start state recognized; no fault protection trip
scenarios.l2: CB CLOSE → start detection → acceleration → start supervision reset
scenarios.l3: High starting current followed by expected decay/acceleration
scenarios.fallback: If start element absent: CB close + current envelope + speed/process feedback if available

scenarios.l1: Start timer remains active or start-time limit reached
scenarios.l2: CB CLOSE → high current persists beyond expected start window → alarm/trip
scenarios.l3: Starting current remains high with insufficient decay/acceleration
scenarios.fallback: If timer bit absent: duration of elevated current + speed/auxiliary evidence

scenarios.l1: Locked-rotor element or start timeout operates
scenarios.l2: Start → high current persists → locked-rotor/start timeout → trip
scenarios.l3: Near-constant high current with little/no acceleration evidence
scenarios.fallback: If locked-rotor bit absent: current duration + absence of speed increase + thermal rise

scenarios.l2: Running state → current rises → jam detection → trip
scenarios.l3: Sudden sustained current increase from running state
scenarios.fallback: If jam element absent: current step/rise + running-state SOE + speed/process feedback

scenarios.l2: Thermal pickup → delay → trip
scenarios.l3: Sustained RMS current and temperature/thermal accumulation
scenarios.fallback: If thermal signal absent: current trend + temperature + duration

scenarios.l2: Detection → timer → alarm/trip
scenarios.l3: One phase current/voltage abnormal relative to others
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated element absent: compare IA/IB/IC and VA/VB/VC; derive negative sequence

scenarios.l2: Pickup → timer/thermal limit → trip/alarm
scenarios.l3: Elevated I2/I1 and phase unbalance
scenarios.fallback: If element absent: calculate sequence components from synchronized three-phase current waveforms

scenarios.l1: Differential or phase fault protection operates
scenarios.l2: Pickup → trip → motor CB open
scenarios.l3: High fault current, voltage depression, differential imbalance
scenarios.fallback: If differential unavailable: phase OC + current/voltage waveform + feeder topology

scenarios.ansi: Earth fault / differential / sensitive earth fault
scenarios.l2: Pickup → trip → breaker opening
scenarios.l3: Residual current / zero-sequence behavior + phase-earth voltage response
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated earth element absent: derive residual current from phase currents + topology

scenarios.ansi: Earth fault; directional earth fault; distance
scenarios.l2: START → timer/zone → trip → CB open
scenarios.l3: 3I0/residual current + phase voltage depression; direction/impedance supports protected zone
scenarios.fallback: If zone/direction signal missing: phasors + sequence components + impedance trajectory + topology

scenarios.l2: START → timer/zone → trip
scenarios.l3: Two phase currents rise; corresponding voltages depress; negative sequence increases
scenarios.fallback: If zone signal absent: calculate apparent impedance and inspect phase current/voltage relationship

scenarios.l2: START → zone/timer → trip
scenarios.l3: Three-phase current rise + voltage depression
scenarios.fallback: If distance/zone bit absent: V/I phasors + impedance trajectory + topology

scenarios.l1: Relay sees fault current but direction/zone may restrain
scenarios.l2: Neighboring protection/backup sequence indicates external location
scenarios.l3: High current with direction/impedance inconsistent with protected zone
scenarios.fallback: If directional/zone data missing: topology + neighboring relay SOE + current/voltage comparison

scenarios.ansi: High-impedance fault detection; sensitive earth fault
scenarios.l1: Special HIF/HIZ element may operate; conventional OC may not
scenarios.l2: Detection → alarm/trip if configured
scenarios.l3: Low/moderate fault current, abnormal residual/sequence signature, possible intermittent behavior
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated HIF element absent: residual/sequence current + voltage distortion + intermittent waveform pattern

scenarios.l2: Repeated short pickups/operations around intermittent events
scenarios.l3: Short residual-current bursts with repeated extinction/restrike behavior
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated signal absent: identify repeated synchronized 3I0/residual bursts + voltage disturbance

scenarios.l2: Trip → CB OPEN → dead time → CB CLOSE → no repeat trip
scenarios.l3: Fault signature exists before first opening and disappears after reclose
scenarios.fallback: If autoreclose bit absent: infer from CB open/close SOE and disappearance of fault signature

scenarios.l2: Trip → open → reclose → protection pickup/trip again
scenarios.l3: Fault signature persists after reclose
scenarios.fallback: If autoreclose signal absent: repeated CB open/close + repeated protection operation

scenarios.l1: Fault protection operates immediately following close
scenarios.l2: CB CLOSE → immediate protection pickup/trip
scenarios.l3: Fault current and voltage collapse start essentially at energization
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated SOTF logic absent: CB close timing + immediate fault waveform

scenarios.l1: Bus differential operates; multiple zones/feeders may trip
scenarios.l2: Bus protection trip → lockout/master trip → multiple breakers open
scenarios.l3: Simultaneous current contributions from multiple circuits + bus voltage collapse
scenarios.fallback: If bus differential bit absent: correlate multiple feeder/incomer currents, directions, bus voltage and breaker SOE

scenarios.scenario: External feeder fault with bus restraint
scenarios.l1: Feeder protection operates; bus differential should remain restrained
scenarios.l2: Feeder trip → feeder CB opens while bus remains energized
scenarios.l3: High feeder current but no credible bus-wide differential fault
scenarios.fallback: If bus differential data missing: feeder current + bus voltage + other breaker states + neighboring relay SOE

scenarios.scenario: Bus differential false operation / CT issue
scenarios.l1: Bus differential trip without matching physical bus fault
scenarios.l2: Multiple breakers trip but event sequence does not match a bus fault
scenarios.l3: No credible bus-fault waveform; CT mismatch/distortion possible
scenarios.fallback: If CT diagnostic unavailable: compare all CT waveforms, current balance/polarity and external-fault sequence

scenarios.l2: Pickup → trip → generator breaker opens
scenarios.l3: High differential/fault current + terminal voltage depression
scenarios.fallback: If differential unavailable: phase OC + current/voltage + sequence + topology

scenarios.ansi: Earth fault; generator differential; neutral/third-harmonic schemes
scenarios.l2: Pickup → trip → breaker opening
scenarios.l3: Residual/neutral/third-harmonic evidence depending protection scheme
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated element absent: residual current + neutral/terminal voltage + third harmonic if recorded

scenarios.l2: Pickup → delay → alarm/trip
scenarios.l3: P/Q and V/I operating trajectory consistent with loss of excitation
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated signal absent: P/Q + phasor trajectory + voltage/power-angle behavior

scenarios.l2: Pickup → thermal/timer → trip
scenarios.l3: Elevated I2 and sustained phase unbalance
scenarios.fallback: If element absent: calculate I2/I1 from three-phase currents

scenarios.l2: Frequency pickup → timer/load shedding/trip
scenarios.l3: Frequency excursion and rate-of-change
scenarios.fallback: If relay frequency unavailable: derive frequency and df/dt from voltage waveform

scenarios.l2: Detection → trip/blocking logic → breaker response
scenarios.l3: Impedance/power-angle trajectory or voltage-vector shift behavior
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated element absent: impedance trajectory + P/Q oscillation + voltage-angle behavior

scenarios.l2: CB CLOSE while generator is not in expected state → immediate protection response
scenarios.l3: Current appears immediately after unexpected energization; machine pre-event state inconsistent with normal operation
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated logic absent: CB close + pre-event machine state + current surge + voltage response

scenarios.l2: V/Hz pickup → timer → trip/alarm
scenarios.l3: Elevated V/Hz
scenarios.fallback: If stage absent: derive V/Hz from voltage waveform and frequency

scenarios.l2: CB CLOSE → transient → decay → stable
scenarios.l3: Short-duration oscillatory/high-frequency transient synchronized with switching
scenarios.fallback: If switching signal absent: CB SOE + waveform onset/decay

scenarios.l2: Pickup → alarm/trip → CB open
scenarios.l3: Phase/current/neutral imbalance or sustained abnormal voltage/current
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated unbalance signal absent: calculate phase/neutral imbalance from DR

scenarios.l2: Pickup → delay → trip/alarm
scenarios.l3: Sustained elevated voltage
scenarios.fallback: If protection bit absent: calculate RMS and sequence voltages from DR

scenarios.ansi: Trip command; breaker status; current interruption
scenarios.l1: Trip command issued; status changes normally
scenarios.l2: Trip command → 52a/52b transition → current interruption
scenarios.l3: Current drops to zero after expected opening; breaker status agrees
scenarios.fallback: If breaker status unavailable: current interruption + neighboring device SOE + voltage/state change

scenarios.scenario: Breaker fails to open after trip
scenarios.l2: Primary trip command → expected clearing time expires → current persists → backup trip
scenarios.l3: Fault current persists after local trip command; local status fails to change
scenarios.fallback: If BF bit absent: trip command + persistent current + unchanged status + subsequent upstream breaker trip

scenarios.l2: Trip command issued but no expected breaker response
scenarios.l3: No current interruption and/or breaker status unchanged; DC/trip voltage abnormal if recorded
scenarios.fallback: If supervision signal absent: command/status mismatch + current persistence + DC/trip voltage if available

scenarios.l1: Failure to open or close as commanded
scenarios.l2: Command → no status transition within expected time
scenarios.l3: Current/state remains inconsistent with command
scenarios.fallback: If dedicated monitoring absent: SOE command/status mismatch + current/voltage evidence

scenarios.scenario: Local Breaker Backup / LBB cascade clearing
scenarios.l1: Local BF/LBB function starts or operates
scenarios.l2: Primary feeder/transformer breaker trip command → local CB fails → BF timer → upstream/incomer/bus-side breakers trip
scenarios.l3: Fault current persists after primary trip and disappears only after backup breakers open
scenarios.fallback: If BF/LBB signal absent: reconstruct using trip command, 52 status, current persistence, BF timer-equivalent interval and upstream breaker trips
scenarios.final_class: FAULT + LOCAL BREAKER FAILURE + LBB/CASCADE CLEARING

scenarios.scenario: Cascade trip caused by protection coordination
scenarios.l1: Primary protection may fail/block; backup stage operates
scenarios.l2: Primary device → no/failed clearing → backup relay operates → additional breaker(s) trip
scenarios.l3: Fault persists through first clearing attempt and clears after backup device operation
scenarios.fallback: If backup stage signal absent: SOE order + current persistence + sequential breaker openings

scenarios.scenario: Bus/incomer trip caused by downstream feeder breaker failure
scenarios.ansi: Feeder protection + breaker failure + incomer/bus protection
scenarios.l1: Feeder protection trips first; incomer/bus-side protection trips later
scenarios.l2: Feeder trip command → feeder CB fails → BF/LBB → incomer/bus breaker trips
scenarios.l3: Feeder fault current continues until incomer/bus breaker opens
scenarios.fallback: If feeder BF signal missing: time-order + feeder 52 status + current persistence + incomer trip

scenarios.l1: One primary fault declaration followed by backup trips
scenarios.l2: Primary breaker command → failed clearing → backup trips in defined hierarchy
scenarios.l3: Single fault signature persists while successive breakers open; no independent bus-fault signature
scenarios.fallback: If topology/logic signals missing: reconstruct from SOE timestamps and current discontinuity after each breaker opening
scenarios.final_class: CASCADE / BACKUP CLEARING — NOT AUTOMATICALLY A BUS FAULT

scenarios.scenario: Successful backup clearing after primary breaker failure
scenarios.l1: Primary protection operates; local breaker fails; backup protection succeeds
scenarios.l2: Primary trip → BF interval → backup breaker(s) trip → fault current clears
scenarios.l3: Current persists during BF interval then collapses after backup breaker opening
scenarios.fallback: If BF signal absent: current persistence + breaker sequence + final clearing location
scenarios.final_class: BREAKER FAILURE WITH SUCCESSFUL BACKUP CLEARING

scenarios.l1: VT supervision may alarm/block voltage-dependent elements
scenarios.l2: Voltage supervision change → protection block/alarm → no matching current fault
scenarios.l3: One/more voltage channels collapse while currents/power/system state do not support a real voltage fault
scenarios.fallback: If VT supervision absent: phase-voltage comparison + sequence voltage + current/power continuity + independent voltage source

scenarios.l1: Protection may respond abnormally during high current
scenarios.l2: Protection operation occurs during high external/through-fault event
scenarios.l3: CT waveform clipping/distortion/asymmetry and current mismatch during high through-current
scenarios.fallback: If CT flag absent: raw waveform + both-side current comparison + external-fault evidence

scenarios.l1: Unexpected differential or imbalance may appear
scenarios.l2: Mismatch appears during otherwise balanced/known conditions
scenarios.l3: Current magnitude/phase relationship inconsistent between channels
scenarios.fallback: If diagnostic unavailable: compare channels across healthy load and known faults; cross-check independent relay/meter records

scenarios.l2: SOE order contradicts expected protection sequence or command originates without valid initiating condition
scenarios.l3: DR may show no corresponding physical fault
scenarios.fallback: If logic signals unavailable: compare relay events, breaker commands, SCADA commands and DR physical state

scenarios.l2: Trip sequence exists but independent evidence does not support fault
scenarios.l3: DR lacks corresponding physical signature or contradicts declared condition
scenarios.fallback: Cross-check independent relay, neighboring device, CT/VT health, breaker status and topology

lbb_cascade_logic.question: Was there a credible primary fault signature?
lbb_cascade_logic.if_yes: Identify fault type and probable location
lbb_cascade_logic.if_no: Check protection/control/measurement issue before assuming fault

lbb_cascade_logic.question: Did primary protection START/OPERATE?
lbb_cascade_logic.if_no: Use DR/SOE/neighbouring relay if signal missing

lbb_cascade_logic.question: Was a trip command issued to local breaker?
Did local breaker status change correctly?
Did fault current disappear after local breaker opening?
Did breaker-failure/LBB logic start or time out?
lbb_cascade_logic.if_no: Infer from elapsed time + persistent current + backup trip sequence

lbb_cascade_logic.question: Did upstream/incomer/bus-side breaker(s) trip afterward?
lbb_cascade_logic.if_no: If not, investigate incomplete backup action

lbb_cascade_logic.question: Did fault current disappear only after backup breaker(s) opened?
Is there independent evidence of a bus fault?
lbb_cascade_logic.if_yes: Do not automatically label feeder LBB as bus fault; classify actual bus evidence separately
lbb_cascade_logic.if_no: Classify as downstream feeder fault + LBB

lbb_cascade_logic.question: Final classification
lbb_cascade_logic.meaning: Avoid 'multiple breaker trip = bus fault' error

fallback_methodology.primary: START/PICKUP, OPERATE, TRIP, stage, phase, direction, zone
fallback_methodology.fallback: Related protection function(s) and available status bits
fallback_methodology.rule: Never infer a missing relay bit as if it existed.

fallback_methodology.primary: Protection sequence, timers, trip commands, breaker status
fallback_methodology.fallback: Relay event timestamps + SCADA/SOE + neighboring relays

fallback_methodology.primary: Measured currents, voltages, sequence, impedance, P/Q, frequency, temperature, harmonics
fallback_methodology.fallback: Derive quantities mathematically from raw waveforms
fallback_methodology.rule: Waveform-derived evidence may replace a missing dedicated indication.

fallback_methodology.primary: Breaker positions, bus/feeder connectivity, source directions
fallback_methodology.fallback: Neighboring relay events and switching state
Trip command + unchanged breaker status + persistent current + delayed backup trip
fallback_methodology.rule: Do not call a cascade a bus fault without independent bus-fault evidence.

fallback_methodology.fallback: CB close + asymmetric/distorted decaying current waveform
fallback_methodology.rule: Harmonics support the diagnosis but are not mandatory.

fallback_methodology.fallback: Partial evidence with explicit missing channels

rca_taxonomy.meaning: Independent evidence agrees across relay/SOE/DR or equivalent fallback paths
rca_taxonomy.minimum: At least two independent evidence classes; preferably L1+L2+L3

rca_taxonomy.meaning: Strong physical and chronological evidence but one important signal/channel is missing
rca_taxonomy.minimum: Strong DR/SOE or equivalent independent evidence

rca_taxonomy.meaning: Plausible but insufficient to distinguish from alternatives
Declared by relay/event but physical evidence does not support it
Primary fault exists but local breaker fails and backup clears
rca_taxonomy.minimum: Persistent current after local trip + backup breaker clearing

rca_taxonomy.meaning: Multiple breakers operate as consequence of failed/backup clearing
CT/VT/channel problem likely explains protection declaration
Trip or blocking sequence inconsistent with physical fault
Protection operation lacks physical/system support after instrumentation/control checks
rca_taxonomy.minimum: Relay declaration contradicted by independent evidence
